intro.caption: Lesson 2-7 — dividing decimals. Max Maxwell says his $38.40 giveaway pool only made 2.4 prize cards! Clip Squad stages a studio audit to split their own prize pool and expose his broken math.

balloons.t: We recovered $38.40 for our fan giveaway. Every mini-card holds $1.60.
Max claims 38.4 ÷ 1.6 is 2.4 cards! That smells fishy.
I tried 4.8 ÷ 0.6! I moved 0.6 to 6, got 4.8 ÷ 6 = 0.8! Replay!
You only shifted the divisor! Move BOTH decimal points the same places!

pages.caption: To keep an equivalent division, shift the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend.

balloons.t: Make the divisor a whole number first. Then shift the dividend the exact same way.
Now let's split our $38.40 pool into $1.60 mini-cards. No missing cards!
Chat is watching! Get the exact card count!
My audit script checks every division by multiplying back to the start.
Wait — if a divisor has TWO decimal places, we shift BOTH numbers twice?
My math is golden! $45.60 in $0.80 stickers is 5.7 stickers. Deal with it!
Three audit locks on that board, Max. Watch us crack every one.
Twenty-four mini-cards packed, Max's math exposed, and Dex only replayed one slip!

win.caption: Making the divisor a whole number turns any decimal division into a whole-number division with the exact same quotient.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Shift Both Points
gates.prompt: Pick the right tool: rewrite each division so the divisor is a whole number, shifting both numbers equally.
hints: Conceptual: multiplying both the dividend and divisor by 10 (or 100) keeps the quotient exactly the same.
Procedural: count how many places the divisor's decimal point must move right to make a whole number, then move the dividend's point the same number of places.

steps: The divisor 0.9 needs 1 shift right to become 9.

options.fb: You shifted the divisor 1 place, but left the dividend 18.9 unchanged.
You shifted the dividend, but the divisor 6.3 is still a decimal!
Both points must move to the RIGHT, not opposite directions.

fb.msg: That's 4.8 ÷ 6 — Dex's mistake! Shift BOTH points 1 place to get 48 ÷ 6.
You shifted the dividend 2 places instead of 1. Move both 1 place: 48 ÷ 6.

items.fbDefault: Shift both decimal points 1 place right to make 48 ÷ 6, then divide.

gates.pass: Both points shifted together: 189 ÷ 63 = 3 and 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Dex crosses out his 0.8.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Split the Pool
gates.prompt: Use equivalent division and the Decimal Division Algorithm to count the giveaway cards and studio supplies.
hints: Conceptual: after shifting both decimal points, you are dividing whole numbers.
Procedural: shift both decimal points right until the divisor is whole, then divide normally.

items.aria: number of 1.60 dollar cards from 38.40 dollars

fb.msg: 2.4 is 38.4 ÷ 16 — that's Max's trick! Shift 38.4 right too to get 384 ÷ 16.
Too big! Both numbers only need 1 shift right: 384 ÷ 16.

items.fbDefault: Shift both 1 place right to get 384 ÷ 16, then divide.

items.aria: number of 1.5 meter LED strips in 22.5 meters

fb.msg: 1.5 is 22.5 ÷ 15. Don't forget to shift the dividend's point right too!
Move each point only 1 place right: 225 ÷ 15.

gates.pass: 24 gift cards and 15 LED strips! Max's '2.4 cards' excuse is officially busted.

gates.title: Gate 3 · The Heist Check
gates.prompt: Verify the division by multiplying back, and handle a divisor with two decimal places.
hints: Conceptual: quotient × original divisor must equal the original dividend.
Procedural: if the divisor has 2 decimal places (like 0.75), shift BOTH numbers 2 places right — annex a zero on the dividend if needed.

steps: 0.24 has 2 decimal places, so shift both 2 places right: 720 ÷ 24 = 30.

options.fb: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, not the dividend by the divisor.

items.label: To rewrite 19.5 ÷ 0.75, the new dividend is:
items.aria: new whole-number dividend when shifting 19.5 two places right

fb.msg: 0.75 needs 2 shifts to become 75, so 19.5 also needs 2 shifts. Annex a zero!
You must shift the dividend the same 2 places as 0.75.

items.fbDefault: Shift 19.5 two places right by annexing one zero.

gates.pass: 24 × 1.6 = 38.4, and 19.5 becomes 1950! Mei's audit screen flashes green.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Expose Max
gates.prompt: Crack all three locks on Max's studio board to recover the full giveaway.
hints: Conceptual: shifting both decimal points multiplies both numbers by 10 or 100, keeping the division equivalent.
Procedural: make the divisor whole, shift the dividend the exact same number of places (annex zeros if needed), then divide.

items.label: Lock 1 · Fix Max's claim: 45.6 ÷ 0.8 =

fb.msg: 5.7 is 45.6 ÷ 8 — Max forgot to shift the dividend too!
Both numbers only shift 1 place right: 456 ÷ 8.

items.fbDefault: Shift both 1 place right to get 456 ÷ 8, then divide.

items.label: Lock 2 · 12.6 ÷ 0.35 =

fb.msg: You shifted 12.6 only 1 place instead of 2. Annex a zero: 1260 ÷ 35.

items.fbDefault: Shift both 2 places right (1260 ÷ 35), then divide.

items.q: Lock 3 · Why does shifting both decimal points the same places keep the quotient equal?

options.t: It makes the quotient smaller every time
options.fb: Dividing by a number less than 1 actually makes the quotient larger!

options.t: It only works when numbers end in zero
options.fb: It works for any decimals — just annex zeros when needed.

options.t: It multiplies both numbers by the same power of 10

options.fb: Changing only the divisor breaks the division and gives the wrong answer.

gates.pass: CLICK! All three locks pop open — 57 stickers, 36, and equivalent division proven. Max slips out the back!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-7 — what the giveaway heist taught us
rows: Move the decimal point the same number of places to the right in BOTH the divisor and the dividend.
If the dividend runs out of digits when shifting (like 12.6 → 1260), add zeros at the end.
Quotient × original divisor = original dividend. 24 × 1.6 = 38.4 proves the division.
Shifting only the divisor turns 45.6 ÷ 0.8 into 45.6 ÷ 8 = 5.7 — ten times too small!
journal.quote: "Never trust a rival who only moves one decimal point." — Blink

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-7 (Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers making the divisor a whole number via equivalent division, annexing zeros, and checking with multiplication.
standards: Fluently divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm
